additions.site_name: GDS Shaoguan Computing Cluster, Baitu Industrial Park, Qujiang
additions.name: GDS Shaoguan Computing Cluster (韶关万国数据算力集群) — data-centre campus development

status.summary: On 26 October 2026 the Shaoguan Ecology and Environment Bureau published, with its acceptance notice (accepted 23 October), the EIA report form of the 万国数据韶关220千伏输变电工程 filed by the GDS project company 韶关市万国云耀数据科技有限公司. The filing names the GDS Shaoguan computing cluster (韶关万国数据算力集群) in the Baitu industrial park, Qujiang, as the sole load of a new dedicated 220 kV substation (GDS I) and describes the GDS data centre to be built there with T-BLOCK modules. Phase 1 of the substation (2x120 MVA, 112.6 MW maximum load) is planned for December 2026 and phase 2 (225.4 MW in total) for late 2027 or April 2028. This dated regulatory filing identifies the data-centre project and supports announced status only: it concerns grid-connection infrastructure, is not development consent for the data centre, and establishes no data-centre construction, completion or operation. Loads and dates are substation plans, not IT capacity.

locator.precision: Centre of the proposed GDS I (万国I站) 220 kV user substation that the GDS project company is building to supply only the GDS Shaoguan computing cluster, printed in its October 2026 EIA. It marks the cluster through its dedicated grid intake in the Baitu industrial park; it is not a data-hall centre, parcel centroid, entrance, campus boundary or construction extent.
locator.identity_review: The EIA cover names the project 万国数据韶关220千伏输变电工程 and the builder 韶关市万国云耀数据科技有限公司 (the acceptance notice writes 韶关市云耀数据科技有限公司); its text names the supply range 韶关万国数据算力集群 and describes GDS's data centre and T-BLOCK technology, the same Baitu cluster that the thirty-fourth update held with a reopen condition asking for this user-substation point. The July 2026 Baitu 220 kV EIA routes its cable along park roads into the 220 kV GDS user station (万国用户站) through a cable channel inside that station; its end point, after the GCJ-02 inverse, lies 71.5 m from this centre, so both grid filings describe the same station. The point is the published DMS converted to decimal without a datum shift. The same filing's Tanjie line end, read as WGS84, falls inside the walled Tanjie substation yard on Esri imagery, while the June and July EIAs' GCJ-02-like values fall about 600 m away. On undated imagery the point lies in a cleared earthworks tract just east of the park's factory blocks. Details: sources/research-countries-2026-10-27-cn-gd-gx-fj-p3-gds-shaoguan-baitu-geometry-facts.json.
locator.uncertainty_reason: No datum or positional accuracy is stated. The WGS84 reading rests on a qualitative imagery check of a second point in the same filing (the Tanjie line end) and on agreement within 72 m with the GCJ-02-corrected point of the July grid EIA. None of the filings outlines the data-centre property, so the substation's offset from the data-centre buildings, and whether it lies inside their parcel, are unknown. Decimal places are transcription precision.

additions.site_identity_review: LGA4 is DataBank's planned second data center at 2000 Corporate Drive, Orangeburg, Town of Orangetown, Rockland County. That is the campus the existing site curated:databank-orangeburg-campus-2000-corporate-drive represents. The site was added on 23 October 2026 (us-midwest-east-p2, published in the sixtieth update) with one project, LGA3 existing operations, and was already named 'LGA3 and LGA4'. DataBank's campus page says the 34-acre campus 'is home to LGA3 and LGA4' and lists both at 2000 Corporate Dr. The LGA4 page says LGA4 'will be our second facility on our Orangeburg, NY Campus'. LGA4 is therefore a new project on the existing site, not a new site. It was held on 23 October only because a second project could not be added to a site created in the same update, and that hold's reopen condition (the site in the base dataset plus a dated DataBank or government record naming the expansion) is now met.

status.summary: DataBank's news item of 1 September 2026 describes 'DataBank's existing facility and proposed expansion in Orangeburg' and 'DataBank's 45-megawatt Orangeburg campus project'. It says the Town of Orangetown exempted the DataBank project from its new moratorium 'because it is already in the approval process'. That is a dated operator disclosure of the proposed expansion while it is under review. DataBank's campus and LGA4 pages identify the expansion as LGA4, the campus's planned second data center: 55,000 sq ft of data center space and 10 MW of critical power by design. The DEC's sitemap lists a Town of Orangetown SEQR notice titled 'DataBank Orangeburg Phase Two' in the Environmental Notice Bulletin of 2 September 2026, and DataBank's 10 August 2026 news item (existing evidence f87752e1) says the expansion was undergoing a full environmental impact study before it could go to the Orangetown Planning Board. No Planning Board approval, permit or construction is established, so the status is announced as of 1 September 2026. The 45 MW is a campus power figure, not IT load. The 10 MW is a planned design figure.
